newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian bank Celje to merge with bank Noricum.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian bank Celje to merge with bank Noricum.

text.p: Slovenian bank Banka Celje said on Tuesday it would merge with bank Noricum on December 31 in order to boost its market share.
The new bank will carry the name of Banka Celje.
"The main reason for the merger with Noricum was our intention to open a branch in Ljubljana and increase our market share," Niko Kac, general manager of Banka Celje, told Reuters.
Kac said the bank expected to increase its market share to 5.7 percent from 3.8 percent by 1998. Bank Noricum has a 0.4 percent share of the Slovenian market.
"Bank Celje will benefit by gaining Noricum's seat in Ljubljana, its clients and its employees, while Noricum will become much stronger and less vulnerable," Kac added.

Several Slovenian banks have recently annnounced merger plans in order to cut their operational costs and increase efficiency as they prepare for tougher competition once the sector is thrown open to foreign players.

Parliament is expected to pass a new bank law next year, enabling foreign banks to establish branches in Slovenia in line with European Union regulations. Currently foreign banks can only set up subsidiaries, requiring big capital outlays.
Analysts have forecast there will be more mergers before the end of this year.
Slovenia, the smallest of the former Yugoslav republics with a population of just two million people, has 29 registered banks, most of them small.
